A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ACIP by the same authors. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite the changed title, organization, and layout.

before.justification: V1 reports original ACIP experiments across multiple LLMs, including perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, quantization, fine-tuning, and component ablations in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds original efficiency measurements and a layer-reset ablation in Appendix D.

M1.justification: V2 adds an optional compression rule in Appendix D.3: restore masks and disable adapters for layers whose factorization would not save parameters, recovering the original model at full size. The default SVD reparametrization, sparsity objective, iterative scoring, and compression procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4, WikiText-2, the same seven zero-shot evaluation tasks, and the same illustrative generation prompts. The added efficiency measurements and layer-reset experiment do not introduce a new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Dobi-SVD without remapping and includes SVD magnitude pruning, previously examined only in v1's appendix. New Table A3 compares fine-tuned ASVD and SVD-LLM against ACIP, a comparison explicitly omitted in v1. These substantially broaden the reported comparator set; the external-method scores are attributed to prior publications.

E3.justification: V2 introduces an efficiency protocol using generation length 64 and batch size 64, plus FLOP measurement with fvcore at input length 512. Appendix B also narrows the stated fine-tuning budget from 20K–25K to 25K steps. These changes do not establish that retained benchmark results were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 adds stage-wise efficiency and inference analysis, while D.3/Figure A10 tests whether resetting incompressible layers reduces the adapter-induced performance penalty. These are targeted additions; the earlier adapter, stopping, score-map, post-tuning, and layer-selection analyses remain under matched or renumbered references.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's efficiency statistics are point measurements, not an added uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Shared Table 1 rows, Table A2 values, and the quantization results remain unchanged. V2 adds baseline and fine-tuning comparison entries, layer-reset results, and efficiency findings. Table A5 newly reports 1594.99 tokens/s at 40% size versus 2447.75 for the original model, despite smaller checkpoint size and lower memory use.

T1.justification: Table A5 adds qualitative asymptotic cost expressions for ACIP's three stages, including compression scaling with layer count and input dimension. The underlying SVD and sparsity mathematics remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is supplied. The adapter-concatenation equations provide an equivalent implementation of the existing factorization.

C1.justification: The central claims of arbitrary-size compression from one optimization run, competitive factorization-based performance, and compatibility with quantization remain. V2 adds an explicit first-method claim for real-time arbitrary-size compression without recalibration and drops v1's unqualified claim that no hyperparameter tuning is required.

C2.justification: Remark 2.2 explicitly explains how calibration loss and data determine feature importance. Appendix D.1 acknowledges that the measured compressed models do not achieve inference-speed gains and discusses factorization overhead and possible optimization. The existing limitations concerning larger models and unexplored modalities remain.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the forthcoming-code notice with stated code and ACIP-model availability and specific access links. It also explicitly identifies the next-token negative-log-likelihood loss, explains merging SVD factors and adapters for inference, and documents efficiency-measurement settings. These substantially improve the supplied access and implementation information.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning through an any-size pre-training discussion covering Once-for-All, MatFormer, Matryoshka representations, and Gemma 3n, presenting ACIP as a cheaper post-training alternative. It also incorporates Dobi-SVD and additional structured-pruning, quantization, and distillation literature while retaining the earlier low-rank and rate-distortion connections.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten around two problems and their solutions, and the method exposition more explicitly separates scoring from compression. Related work moves after experiments, comparison results receive a separate subsection, and computational considerations and an appendix contents page are added. The title and contribution narrative also change.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text from two columns to one and redesigns typography and algorithm presentation. A workflow diagram replaces the introductory trade-off plot, Figure 2 highlights expensive versus cheap stages, Table 1 expands, and Tables A3/A5 and Figure A10 are added. Existing appendix displays are extensively relocated and reformatted.

improvement.justification: The added efficiency measurements, layer-reset ablation, broader comparisons, and code/model access information improve practical assessment and reproducibility while retaining the main evidence. The gains have limits: fine-tuning comparisons use different training corpora, and the blanket superiority wording overstates Table 1, where Dobi-SVD achieves lower C4 perplexity at 80% size (10.01 versus ACIP's 10.92).
